Can some one ELI5 about what bump/slide thing is and how they are a restriction? And maybe what select fire is? I have no idea what they are..

Select fire is traditionally associated with "assault rifles." It allows you to select from semi-auto to firing multiple rounds with a single trigger pull. Frequently multiple rounds means full-auto, but can also mean burst fire (whereby 3 shot burst is fairly common). It's called select fire because you select the mode of firing per trigger pull.

A bump/slide stock is a special stock which uses the weapon's natural recoil to cause the trigger to bounce against your finger. They take practice to use well and accuracy generally suffers more so than full-auto, whereby accuracy already suffers with full-auto. Imagine your finger fixed in space. Now imagine the weapon bouncing back and forth against your finger, causing the trigger to be pulled. Repeat.

There is also something called bump fire which is the manual method of rocking the weapon against your trigger finger. It's very difficult to do and takes practice. Even then it's not terribly reliable. Accuracy super sucks.
